messages:
tess: FYI, got a support ticket — workspace-scoped request hit shared pool even though customer has a private endpoint and dedicated capacity.
kevin: Oof. Do we have the request id + headers + routing trace?
alex: Pulled telemetry, minimal headers below.
alex: ```
Request-ID: r-99b1
Host: api.redwood.dev
X-Workspace: ws-221
X-Private-Endpoint: true
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
``` 
alex: Router chose shared-pool-eu initially, then a rewrite to dedicated-ws-221 failed capacity and we fell back. Client never saw a reason header.
maria: Hmm. Our expected precedence is: private endpoint assertion -> tenant binding -> vpc mapping -> shared. Why did gateway attempt shared first? Are we treating workspace header as hint somewhere?
sam: Current behavior: X-Workspace is treated as a hint unless tenant-config.bind=true or the endpoint explicitly asserts. Private endpoints should assert binding but there are edge cases.
kevin: Gateway does a tenant-cache lookup to confirm binding. If cache-miss, gateway treats header as hint and proceeds. I see a cache-miss for ws-221 at 09:12:33 in the trace.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: starting rolling deploy gateway v2.14 by @kevin
tess: @kevin can you confirm config-store read returned binding=false or absent?
kevin: Confirmed. Cache miss -> slower config-store read returned bind=false (old config). So gateway didn't consider the workspace as asserted.
maria: We need a fix that avoids a control-plane RTT for hot private endpoints. Proposal: control-plane should inject an asserted header that gateway can verify cryptographically.
sam: Agreed, but we must prevent forging. HMAC with control-plane key + short TTL should be fine.
alex: POC header format:
```
X-Pool-Assert: dedicated-ws-221
X-Pool-Assert-Sig: base64(hmac_sha256(key, request_id||pool||ts||allow_fallback))
``` 
alex: Gateway verification logic:
```
if X-Pool-Assert present:
  if verify_sig(): route to asserted pool (skip tenant-cache)
  else: log warning and continue normal routing
else:
  normal precedence (tenant-cache -> vpc -> shared)
```
kevin: That would eliminate the extra control-plane lookup for validated private endpoint traffic. Must ensure signature payload includes tenant id so we can assert token owner matches.
tess: Console UX: surface a routing badge like "asserted" with a tooltip: "Routed due to X-Pool-Assert verified signature". Also add link to binding config and last-sync timestamp.
maria: Telemetry: add fields route_reason and pool_asserted (bool) to traces and billing metrics so we can split dedicated vs shared usage for billing and quota checks.
sam: Edge-case: in canary scenarios we might intentionally route a fraction of traffic to shared even with assertion. Sig should support allow_fallback flag and max_fallbacks_per_minute to express that policy.
kevin: We'll include allow_fallback and a TTL in the sig payload. Gateway should also emit fallback reasons (e.g., capacity, quota) into response headers for easier debugging.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: gateway v2.14 paused due to increased CPU, investigating
alex: Immediate short-term mitigation: add X-Routing-Reason header on fallback (e.g., X-Routing-Reason: fallback:capacity) so support can tell customers why they saw shared.
maria: Also add an internal /replay endpoint that re-evaluates routing decisions against current cache for SRE debugging (internal RBAC only).
sam: I'll prototype X-Pool-Assert verification and unit tests; add guard to cross-check signature tenant vs auth token tenant and raise alert on mismatch.
kevin: I'll take telemetry + console changes: trace schema change + small console column and tooltip explaining precedence.
tess: Sounds good. We'll write a short RFC for X-Pool-Assert + telemetry. For now, roll the X-Routing-Reason header change to reduce support noise.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: deploy resume scheduled in 8m
tess: Thanks all — follow-up RFC thread to propose sig format, key rotation policy, and replay tooling. Closing for now.
